cs.t: I have a GL.iNet travel router. When I am not travel, it connects to the router's second WAN port. If my main internet goes down, it takes me 30 seconds to tether my phone and failover manually. My carrier detects and throttles hotspot traffic by measuring packets TTL, so I tweaks the router's iptables to dodge that. Typically I get over 400 Mbps. From time to time I get the itch to improve my home network uptime, and I have to keep reminding myself that the current setup is fine.
I have a little WIFI-6 era GL.iNet travel router and it is fantastic, really like their software and hardware.  https://www.gl-inet.com/products/gl-axt1800/
I use a Glinet travel router.
